checks.claim: The balanced space, C, J sign and duality formula are correct.
checks.reason: Direct computation gives J_E(f,g)=(Lambda^-1 g,-Lambda f), with J_E^*=-J_E, J_E^2=-I and ||J_E||=1. Also <(u,v),J_E(f,g)>_E=<Lambda^(1/2)u,Lambda^(-1/2)g>-<Lambda^(-1/2)v,Lambda^(1/2)f>=dual(u,g)-dual(f,v), so the stated sign holds. C is the accepted J0 of driver Section1 and is onto L2xL2.

checks.claim: The free massless wave, including frequency zero, preserves omega as a bounded form.
checks.reason: The real even Fourier symbol [[cos,sin/|xi|],[-|xi|sin,cos]] has determinant 1 and tends to [[1,t],[0,1]] at xi=0. A real determinant-1 matrix preserves the 2x2 skew form pointwise, and the sesquilinear form integrates on the real subspace. Bessel coordinates give the bounded symbol of upper-cameron lines 369-370, so density extends the identity to E. Frequency zero is a Lebesgue-null point, and what matters there is the bounded continuous sine quotient. Generator check: omega(Az,w)+omega(z,Aw)=0. This is feasible, and the integral proof remains a later obligation.

checks.claim: B(b) is omega-skew through true duality and is not Hilbert skew on E.
checks.reason: omega(Bz,w)+omega(z,Bw)=dual(u,bf)-dual(f,bu)=int b u f-int b f u=0, since u,f lie in H^(1/2), a subset of L2, and bf,bu lie in L2, a subset of H^(-1/2). Boundedness needs only ||b||_infinity (fixed-mask eq.(4) type bound). <Bz,w>_E is the H^(-1/2) inner product of bu with g, so it is not Hilbert skew, as the target says.

checks.claim: SP1: the bounded strong-state interaction route gives per-rho conservation without differentiating the unbounded generator.
checks.reason: Z(r)=S_E(-r)B(b_rho(r))S_E(r) is uniformly bounded and strongly continuous on the fixed-rho event, using continuity of b_rho in sup norm and strong continuity of S_E. The state U(r,s)z is C^1 in E, omega is bounded bilinear, and Z(r) is omega-skew by conjugation, so omega(Uz,Uw) is constant. Conjugating by symplectic S_E gives P^*JP=J. Fixed-mask Sections5 and 7 identify the Young equation with the ordinary interaction integral on states for h+g m Y_rho. The signed sample potential plays no role in the argument.

checks.reason: M lies in L2 of a separable closed Ctheta path span (driver Section9), and M_rho likewise (source Section3), with Z in L2 on the retaining extension (source eq.(13), I(Phi h)=W(h)). Cauchy-Schwarz gives Bochner existence and ||D_Phi,rho-D_Phi||<=||Phi|| ||M_rho-M||_L2Ctheta. The construction uses only the all-dimensional driver and is not an instantaneous raw mean. Joint-tilt Section2 is used only as a method precedent, as the crosswalk states.

checks.claim: h_Phi,rho=E[Z Y_rho] has the claimed regularity and supplies the source primitive identity.
checks.reason: With Z=I(Phi[Phi]) and Y_rho(t,x)=I(v_rho;t,x), h=<Phi[Phi],v_rho;t,x>_G is deterministic and independent of the auxiliary J. G-norm continuity from eq.(17) and the G-valued derivatives of Section6 make h jointly continuous with all x derivatives, for singular mu too, with no sample suprema. So m_R h lies in C([0,T];C_c^infinity). Testing eqs.(19)-(20) with Z and using absolute Fubini, or the Bochner G integrals of Section5, gives D_Phi,rho(t)=int_0^t S_E(-r)B(m_R h(r))S_E(r)dr on a Schwartz dense set, and boundedness extends it. The proof is a later obligation with no visible obstruction.

checks.claim: Noncentered source convergence holds at fixed parameters in all finite Lp, with no Girsanov step or uniform-Phi inference.
checks.reason: ||D_Phi,rho||_Ctheta<=||Phi|| ||M||_L2Ctheta uniformly in rho (source Section5 contraction), and this Ctheta budget stays bounded even though sup norms of h_rho may diverge. With q=1/theta<2, the bound pC(1+H+|c|x)^q<=c'x^2+C and the uniform square-exponential moments give all evolution moments (fixed-mask Section4 and Section7 argument). Probability convergence on driver balls plus uniform integrability gives Lp convergence. The target keeps Phi fixed and calls the source noncentered, so no centered-Gaussian claim is made.

checks.claim: SP2: preservation passes to the raw flow for all time pairs on one event at fixed c,Phi,R,T, without operator-norm continuity of S_E.
checks.reason: The physical difference is bounded by C_T^2 times the interaction uniform difference, so Lp convergence gives an a.s. uniform-in-(s,t) subsequence. Choosing a countable rho_n sequence gives a countable union of null sets. The bounded form J_E passes to the limit, and no uncountable parameter event is needed. The target explicitly excludes norm continuity of S_E, a static spectral replacement, positivity and block independence.

checks.claim: E/F restriction is available without assuming E is dense in F.
checks.reason: A_F=i M_E Lpsi, A_F i=i M_E, S_F i=i S_E, and (U_A-I)F is contained in closed iE (fixed-mask eq.(8)). Hence U_A i=i U_(M_E) by Young uniqueness, and Young calculus also applies directly on the Banach space E. The covariance driver restricts in the same way, since E[Z A_F]i=i E[Z M_E].

checks.reason: 1=||J_E||=||P^*J_E P||<=||P||^2. P^*JP=J alone does not imply surjectivity, for example S direct-sum S with S a shift on L2xL2 satisfies it and is not onto. Invertibility comes from the accepted Young/free inverse (fixed-mask Section4). The R=1/delta+2, T=1/delta, c=delta^((1-a)/2) instance is one fixed-parameter application per delta, and no uniform source, moment, or noise claim is made. checks.claim: SP4 raw adjoint and residual step: T_m^* exists, is a contraction, and the residual has zero covariance with the fast first driver.
checks.reason: T_m is a test isometry with factors delta^(a-2) delta^2 delta^-a=1 (raw-block eq.(2), C3), so the adjoint between completed null quotients exists with T_m^*T_m=I. E[W(T_m k)W(Phi)]=<k,T_m^*Phi>. A_m is the Lp limit of sums W_m(f_j)A_j with coefficients in W(Ran T_m), so Bochner covariance with W(Phi-T_mT_m^*Phi) vanishes term by term. Temporal blocks remain correlated, and this step does not need independence of blocks. The norm of phi_m can really reach delta^(-a/2)||Phi||, by taking Phi=T_m f with f supported on the block.

checks.claim: SP4 amplitude: unscaled covariance delta^(a/2)H_m, scaled covariance sqrt(delta)H_m, and D_(phi_m)=H_(m,E)(Phi) with no prefactor on 0<=u<=ell_m.
checks.reason: C3 lines 350-351 give E[W_m(f)W(Phi)]=delta^(a/2)int f h_Phi(s_m+delta v,x), so <f,phi_m>_fast=int f h_Phi(s_m+delta v,x) with no prefactor and the same delta argument. C3 eq.(12) at J=0 gives g_delta E[A_m W(Phi)]=sqrt(delta)H_m on u<=ell_m, and upper-young Section4 uses rank-0 C3 in this same way. Dividing by g_delta>0 gives delta^(a/2)H_m, and multiplying by delta^(-a/2) gives H_m. This also reproduces the head identity upper-young eq.(5). Equality is correctly restricted to u<=ell_m, because the raw mean generally continues past the block and T Phi exists only on I.

limitations: This is an AI statement, source, type and application feasibility review, not human verification, a novelty audit or a completed proof of SP1-SP4. Long-proof steps listed under findings.minor were checked for feasibility, not written out in full.

Accepted notes were used as named inputs and not recertified. Their upstream dependencies (for example actual-two-variance-forms.md, compact-sobolev-cutoff.md, fixed-mask-moment-transfer.md, upper-residual-exponential.md and the Friz-Hairer source) are outside the packet.

The tool set had no execution or hashing capability. Python evaluators were not rerun and Lean was not compiled. Control outputs were checked by reading the code and by selected hand calculations only.

The sha256 bindings, byte equality with scientific e51432c and source revision 240f90772131c68fb5fd7ea22ba2bc9d9645cd5d could not be independently verified. The workspace is not a git repository, and JointTilt.lean and its fixture were instead inspected directly and agree with the declared type and use.

The packet has no target-v2 file, so the v2-to-v3 evolution was judged only from target-v1, target-v3 and the honesty note. wiki-recon-v1.json and the cited wiki pages are also absent, and the crosswalk treats them as boundary checks, not inputs.

The GC1-GC3 growing-cone packet is absent. The R=1/delta+2 instance was checked only as a pointwise instance of SP3, and its downstream fit to the growing-cone route was not audited. The future E version of the upper-young product ratio is also not established by this gate.
